items.headline: Artemis III to test Orion docking with test landers in Earth orbit
items.title: NASA’s Artemis III Mission to Test Future Moon Lander Operations
items.scifi_hook: NASA will fly three spacecraft on three rockets to rehearse lunar landing steps in orbit.
items.eli5: Astronauts will practice docking Orion with prototype Moon landers before the real Moon landing.
items.why: It reduces risk and validates hardware for the 2028 crewed Moon landing.
items.text: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history. Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano aboard the Orion spacecraft into low Earth orbit to perform a series of demonstrations with test versions, or test articles, of human landing systems being developed by industry partners Blue Origin and SpaceX. During the planned 14-day mission, crews and flight controllers will practice the rendezvous, docking, habitation, and operational procedures that will be essential when Artemis astronauts begin landing near the Moon’s South Pole in 2028. The mission is designed to reduce risk, validate hardware, and gain operational experience before NASA attempts a crewed lunar landing. “Every piece of this mission in Earth orbit is designed to reduce risk before we put astronauts back on the Moon,” said Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager. “We’re launching three spacecraft on three different rockets and testing how they operate together — something NASA has never attempted. Every lesson we learn here gets us closer to landing on the Moon in 2028.” This graphic shows NASA’s concept of operations for Artemis III. items.headline: NASA revises Artemis architecture, Orion to dock with Starship in high‑Earth orbit
items.title: NASA updates lander plans for Moon landings, finally solves long-festering Orion issue
items.scifi_hook: Orion will meet SpaceX’s Starship far above Earth before heading to the Moon.
items.eli5: NASA plans to connect its crew ship with Starship high above Earth, then travel together to the Moon.
items.why: The new docking plan streamlines the lunar mission and avoids in‑space refueling.
items.text: During a lengthy news conference on Friday, NASA provided a detailed overview of how it plans to return astronauts to the lunar surface as soon as 2028 as part of its Artemis Program. Although much of the information behind these plans has been previously reported at Ars Technica and elsewhere, this marked the first time NASA has laid them out in detail and acknowledged some substantial changes in the architecture. Most notably, for SpaceX's Starship vehicle, the revised plan calls for the Orion spacecraft to dock with the Starship lunar lander in high-Earth orbit before transiting to the Moon. And for Blue Origin, the mission architecture includes four launches of the New Glenn rocket, but no spacecraft-to-spacecraft refuelings. Additionally, the Blue Origin plans allows for the possibility of its Blue Moon lander rendezvousing with Orion in low-Lunar orbit. Read full article Comments

items.headline: NASA, Blue Origin and SpaceX accelerate lunar lander designs for 2028 missions
items.title: NASA, Partners Accelerate Lander Development for 2028 Moon Missions
items.scifi_hook: NASA pushes its commercial partners to fast‑track crew and cargo landers for a Moon base.
items.eli5: NASA is speeding up work with Blue Origin and SpaceX to build Moon landers for astronauts and supplies.
items.why: Accelerated development aims to meet the 2028 deadline for a sustained lunar presence.
items.text: 7 Min Read NASA, Partners Accelerate Lander Development for 2028 Moon Missions As NASA returns humans to the lunar surface and establishes a long-term presence on our closest celestial neighbor, the agency and commercial human landing system providers Blue Origin and SpaceX have streamlined the designs and changed both concepts of operations for its future crewed landers. Since NASA established initial contracts with Blue Origin and SpaceX for crewed missions to the Moon, the agency has redefined Artemis III to demonstrate rendezvous and docking capabilities between test versions of landers from each provider and the agency’s Orion spacecraft in low Earth orbit next year. In parallel, the companies are also developing crew and cargo versions of their landers for near-term Artemis missions. “We are executing President Trump’s National Space Policy to complete the long-awaited return of American astronauts to the lunar surface in 2028 and establish a Moon Base,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “We have a proven foundation in SLS and Orion, along with two lunar landers in development with Blue Origin and SpaceX. But NASA has no intention of sitting idly by as all the pieces come together. That is not how Apollo succeeded, and it is not how the near-impossible is achieved. items.headline: DOE adds helium to critical materials list under Energy Act
items.title: US Department of Energy names helium to critical materials list
items.scifi_hook: Helium, essential for chips, is now officially a strategic U.S. resource.
items.eli5: The government says helium is a vital material and will protect its domestic supply.
items.why: Helium scarcity could threaten semiconductor manufacturing and national security.
items.text: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced Friday that Secretary of Energy Chris Wright has designated helium as a critical material under the Energy Act of 2020. The designation advances the Trump Administration’s commitment to freeing America from reliance on foreign sources of critical materials, strengthening domestic manufacturing, supporting American jobs, and securing the materials essential to U.S. economic and national security, the DOE said. DOE determined that helium meets the statutory definition of a critical material due to its essential role in American manufacturing and growing exposure to supply chain risks. Helium’s unique properties make it indispensable to semiconductor production, with no viable substitutes in many critical applications. Helium in the US is produced as a byproduct of natural gas processing in Kansas, Texas, Wyoming, Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico and Oklahoma. Kansas leads production, with plants refining crude and Grade-A helium from natural gas in fields in the Hugoton and Greenwood areas. items.headline: Bannerman Energy greenlights $353M Etango uranium mine in Namibia
items.title: Bannerman pulls trigger on $353M uranium mine
items.scifi_hook: A joint venture begins building a long‑life uranium mine to fuel the world’s power grids.
items.eli5: Bannerman and China’s CNNC will start building a mine that will produce about 3.5 million pounds of uranium each year.
items.why: It adds secure, diversified uranium supply for global utilities.
items.text: Bannerman Energy (ASX, NSX: BMN; US-OTC: BNNLF) and its Chinese partner CNNC Overseas have approved construction of the Etango uranium project in Namibia, with funding secured without project debt and first production targeted for 2028. The development is expected to cost $353 million before production and deliver an average of 3.5 million lb. of uranium oxide annually. About $64 million has already been spent on early works, leaving roughly $289 million in pre-production spending, Bannerman said in its announcement Friday. The decision moves Etango into full-scale construction after years of studies and preparatory work. “[The FID] is the culmination of more than two decades of exploration, study and disciplined de-risking, and it formally commits the JV to full-scale construction of the world-class Etango Uranium project,” Chamberlain said in a release. “Etango is set to be a long-life, large-scale producer in Namibia’s Erongo region, a highly established uranium province, at a time when the world’s utilities increasingly need secure, diversified supply.” The approval follows a September financing deal with CNNC Overseas, part of China National Nuclear Corp., that secured both construction capital and a buyer for most of Etango’s output. Bannerman owns 55% of the joint venture and CNNC Overseas holds 45%. The venture owns 95% of Etango. items.headline: Record 43.6 Mt of CO₂ stored underground in 2024
items.title: Global underground CO₂ storage hit record 43.6 million metric tons in 2024 alone
items.scifi_hook: Geological reservoirs trapped more carbon this year than ever before, sealing it deep underground.
items.eli5: In 2024, 43.6 million tonnes of carbon dioxide were injected into rock formations, setting a new annual record.
items.why: It demonstrates expanding capacity for carbon removal to limit climate warming.
items.text: The most comprehensive record yet of carbon dioxide stored underground through geological carbon dioxide storage has been published today, revealing that 43.6 million metric tons were sequestered in 2024 alone—a new annual record—and that 421.7 million metric tons have now been stored in the past three decades.
